passages.passageHtml: The company reported record profits this quarter; _____ the CEO announced a freeze on all new hiring, citing "economic uncertainty."
Many historians argue that the treaty prevented a wider war; _____ some critics claim it merely laid the groundwork for future conflicts.
The new software was designed to be user-friendly; _____ the majority of test subjects required additional training to perform basic tasks.
The candidate promised to lower taxes, reduce regulation, and balance the budget; _____, she offered no specific plan to achieve all three goals at once.
The experiment was conducted under strictly controlled conditions; _____, the results varied widely from one trial to the next.
The ancient manuscript was badly damaged by fire; _____ a few key passages remained legible enough to change historians' understanding of the period.
The new manufacturing process reduces waste by 40%; _____ it requires a significant upfront investment in retooling that many small factories cannot afford.
The witness claimed she saw the defendant leave the building at 9:00 PM; _____ security footage showed the defendant had already been in police custody since 8:30 PM.
The training program was voluntary, and most employees chose not to participate; _____, the company saw a 20% increase in productivity across all departments.
The recipe calls for letting the dough rise for at least two hours; _____, the bread will be dense and heavy.
The city's new recycling program initially reduced landfill waste by nearly 30%; _____ the savings in disposal costs have not yet offset the program's startup expenses.
The study found that students who slept at least eight hours scored 15% higher on average; _____ the researchers warned that correlation does not prove causation.
The hurricane destroyed the town's main power grid; _____ emergency generators kept the hospital running for the next 72 hours.
To qualify for the scholarship, a student must maintain a 3.5 GPA and complete 20 volunteer hours; _____ all application materials must be submitted by May 1st.
The manager expected the team to finish the project by Friday; _____ she approved overtime pay for the weekend just in case.

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why B is correct: The first clause says profits were record (positive/expected to lead to hiring). The second clause contradicts that expectation (hiring freeze). "Nevertheless" shows contrast.

Why the distractors are strong:
A. for example – does not fit contrast.
C. consequently – would imply hiring freeze follows from profits (illogical).
D. otherwise – implies a conditional, not contrast.

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why B is correct: The first clause gives one historical view; the second directly opposes it (critics say it laid groundwork for war). "On the contrary" is used to refute or contrast strongly.

Why the distractors are strong:
A. in other words – restates, does not refute.
C. likewise – adds similarity, not opposition.
D. as a result – shows cause-effect, which is illogical here.

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why D is correct: Software claimed to be user-friendly, but test subjects needed extra training – a direct contradiction. "However" signals contrast.

Why the distractors are strong:
A. for instance – gives an example (no example follows).
B. therefore – implies cause-effect (being user-friendly caused need for training? illogical).
C. subsequently – only shows time sequence without contrast.

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why C is correct: The candidate made ambitious promises (positive, forward), but then lacked a plan – a concession or contradiction. "Yet" works like "but" for contrast.

Why the distractors are strong:
A. in addition – adds similar info, not contrast.
B. similarly – compares, not contrasts.
D. hence – shows logical result (no plan would follow from promises? illogical).

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why B is correct: Controlled conditions should produce consistent results, but results varied – unexpected contrast. "Nevertheless" indicates "despite that."

Why the distractors are strong:
A. otherwise – implies alternative condition, not contrast.
C. accordingly – shows logical consequence (consistent results would follow, not varied).
D. consequently – also suggests cause-effect (varied results because of controlled conditions? illogical).

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why C is correct: Fire caused damage (negative), but some passages survived (positive/contrary expectation). "Nevertheless" shows contrast.

Why the distractors are strong:
A. for instance – would introduce an example – no example follows.
B. consequently – would mean "because of fire, passages remained" – illogical.
D. similarly – suggests comparison – no second similar item.

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why A is correct: Benefit (reduces waste) vs. drawback (expensive retooling) – direct contrast. "In contrast" highlights opposing aspects.

Why the distractors are strong:
B. therefore – implies the drawback follows from the benefit – illogical.
C. in addition – adds a similar point, but a drawback is not similar to a benefit here.
D. otherwise – shows condition ("if not, then") – no condition structure.

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why D is correct: Witness says one time (9 PM), but security footage proves impossibility (in custody since 8:30) – contradiction. "However" signals contrast/refutation.

Why the distractors are strong:
A. as a result – would mean footage follows from witness claim – nonsense.
B. for example – gives an example of what? None.
C. meanwhile – suggests simultaneous events – but these contradict, not coexist.

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why B is correct: Employees didn't participate (expected outcome = no improvement), yet productivity rose anyway – unexpected result. "Nonetheless" = "despite that."

Why the distractors are strong:
A. consequently – would mean "because they didn't participate, productivity rose" – false cause.
C. likewise – adds a similar situation – not present.
D. specifically – introduces detail – no detail follows.

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why A is correct: If you don't let dough rise 2+ hours (condition not met), the result is dense bread. "Otherwise" = "if not."

Why the distractors are strong:
B. for example – no example given.
C. in addition – adds info, not a condition.
D. similarly – compares two things, not a warning/condition.

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why A is correct: Positive result (30% less waste) but negative financial outcome (costs not offset). "However" signals this contrast.

Why the distractors are strong:
B. moreover – adds a similar positive point, but second point is negative.
C. for instance – gives an example – no example follows.
D. consequently – implies cost issue results from waste reduction – illogical (separate, not cause-effect).

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why C is correct: Finding (sleep helps scores) but warning (don't assume causation). "Nevertheless" shows concession/contrast.

Why the distractors are strong:
A. likewise – adds a similar finding – no second finding.
B. in other words – restates – warning is a different idea.
D. therefore – would mean "because scores are higher, we conclude causation" – opposite of the warning.

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why D is correct: Power grid destroyed (negative) yet generators worked (positive outcome). "Even so" means "nevertheless."

Why the distractors are strong:
A. as a result – would mean generators worked because of destruction – nonsense.
B. for example – no example.
C. otherwise – implies a conditional ("if not") – no condition here.

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why B is correct: Two requirements (GPA/volunteer) plus a third (May 1st deadline). Simple addition, not contrast or result.

Why the distractors are strong:
A. in contrast – introduces opposite requirement – no opposition.
C. consequently – implies deadline is a result of first requirements – illogical (deadline is separate).
D. similarly – compares two like things – here it's adding a new requirement, not comparing.

questions.questionHtml: Choose the option that correctly completes the sentence.
questions.explanationHtml:
Why A is correct: Expectation (finish by Friday) leads to logical consequence (approve overtime just in case). "Hence" = "for this reason."

Why the distractors are strong:
B. instead – suggests doing the opposite – but overtime is a backup, not an opposite.
C. meanwhile – suggests simultaneous unrelated action – no.
D. for example – no specific example given.
